_about: Settings of `agentcake eval` (agentcake/eval.py, agentcake/evaluation/, plan step S3.9). The thresholds it judges are in eval/thresholds.json (GOAL section 6), not here. No local paths: data that only lives on one machine is named on the command line or in a sources file (eval/sources.example.json).

files._about: Files of a checkout of Agent Cake, relative to the folder that holds the agentcake package: used when neither the command line nor the sources file names them, and skipped with a note when they are not there (an installed wheel has none of them).

short_hash._about: How the sample lists name sessions (eval/README.md): sha256(prefix + id), the first `hex` hex digits. recording: the S1.5 recorder's run id; posthog: S1.5's unit id (a whole session's unit id is its session hash); goal: cake's own session id, for the sessions of a CAKE_HOME listed in truth_goal.jsonl.

truth._about: Answer words of the sample lists. The clean recordings' list: `human` for a clean human recording. The recordings' list: `agent` for an agent's recording, `mixed` for a human and Claude in Chrome taking turns. truth_goal.jsonl: class is the four-layer class the session should get.

lab._about: Our behaviour lab's sessions (bh-lab-1111 and the 11/09 lab) by their label (gt), first matching prefix wins: the group, and the four-layer class and row each should get (Claude in Chrome is AI in a real browser; every Playwright, Puppeteer or CDP run is an automated browser, D17). segment_group: the lab's own three groups for its per-segment table (labcore.gt_group). a2_groups: the groups GOAL A2 names, local agents with answers (Claude in Chrome, headed Playwright moving like a hand). splice_agent / splice_stand_in: the per-segment table's splices, which reproduce the lab's own (bh-lab-1111/splice.py: Claude in Chrome, with a human-like Playwright script standing in for the human). splice_humanlike: the hand-off table's lab_splices, the human-like Playwright scripts as what they are, agents (D17), each spliced with the recorder's real people: a splice's human side is always a real person (the coordinator, 11/13), and Claude in Chrome with those people is recording_splices.

recorded._about: The recorder's agent and hand-off recordings (the recordings' list), by the label of who operated them, as decided on 2026-11-13 under D34 (GOAL A2 to A5 as written, no threshold value changed). a2_labels: GOAL A2's Claude in Chrome, from its side panel or driven by Claude Code: the data set `recorded`, which the gate judges. Every other agent label is a data set of its own, `recorded/<label>`, printed and never judged (the local AI browsers are GOAL T18 to T21's, with their own expectations). Hand-offs are `recorded_handoffs`, judged for A3 to A5 beside the splices.

scoreboard._about: The behaviour layer reported the industry's way (agentcake/evaluation/scoreboard.py, plan step S3.7, decision D36; Akamai's research prototype and AgentShield, research note 21): the evaluable share, recall per agent product, human false positives with their exact interval at `confidence`, precision when agents are each of `prevalences` of all sessions, and every count per site. agent_sources and human_sources: the data sets whose agent or human answers it counts (posthog's answers are reference only, eval/README.md; selfcollect is the recordings we ran ourselves, S9.4, kept apart from people's recorded ones). recording: how each data set recorded input (raw: cake.js's raw events; rrweb: PostHog's recording, without keys, wheel or screen positions): precision pairs a product with the humans recorded the same way. products: the agent product a group or label belongs to (others are their own). sites: the site of a data set whose rows do not name one.

heldout._about: Thresholds set from data (agentcake/evaluation/heldout.py, plan step S3.7, decision D36): each rule listed is fitted from people's segments alone, the candidate that fires most while firing on at most budget of the measured segments of every data set of people; the eval fits it on all the people, and again without each site's people to judge that site (held out by site). Agents are never used, so every agent product is held out by construction. The rule's first condition is the one fitted.

calibration._about: The calibration table (agentcake/evaluation/calibration.py, plan step S3.7, decision D36): the behaviour map of agentcake/data/calibration.json refitted without each data set of sources and checked on it, the packaged map on all of them, and the session percent on every session with an answer; per bin of predicted chance of an agent (bins, [from, to)), how many sessions, the predicted and the actual share, both classes weighted alike; and the Brier score. prior_count: sessions of each class a fitted block is shrunk towards even with (the calibration script uses the same). Real agent products with certain answers are in, each held out by product (sessions.recorded); left_out: the labels of a source that are not, the automation we made to look human: how many of them we record is our choice, not a measurement, and in the fit they would lower every Human's percent by an amount we chose (11/13, agreed with the coordinator).

segments._about: The lab's per-segment test (bh-lab-1111/analyze.py seg_dataset, evaluate, acc; splice.py predict, switch_errors; make_eval.py), unchanged: each segment is an action segment (act) or a one-second window (win); a window's answer is the actor at its middle, an action's at its act time. A window counts 1000 ms of time, an action the wall time since the previous one, at least min_action_ms. band: below it human, above it agent, in between unsure. The logistic regression is the lab's (labcore.fit_lr, pred_lr, vec): features through log1p where listed, a missing indicator per feature, balanced class weights; it trains only when its training data holds both actors.

baselines._about: Whole-session models printed beside Agent Cake's own, never used to judge (research note 11, cake-data/compare_models.py of 2026-11-11, our own code). choudhary: Choudhary et al.'s mouse-event rate over the session's input time (at least min_duration_s) below rate_below a second, or more than teleport_above of the clicks right after a jump (a click whose last move came at most click_window_ms before it, after a jump of more than jump_px in less than jump_ms, or with no move before it). lab_rules_hmm: the lab's rules on each action segment smoothed by its HMM, an agent when at least share of the segments score agent_p or more. superline: @superline-ai/agent-detection 0.0.8 (MIT, Copyright (c) 2025 Superline UG; weights from its dist/esm/model-parameters.js as research note 11 read them): a logistic model on 8 browser and behaviour features, an agent at 0.5 or more; a feature the session did not record is skipped, as superline's scoreFeatures does. environment: each browser feature and the key of the page's recorded environment it is read from.

posthog._about: S1.5's local dataset of tartini.ai's PostHog replays (eval/README.md, `out_dir`): units/<h>.json with the raw-event format and labels. Research note 12's groups of agent units: by the unit's reason, else by a part of its kt link (first match wins), else other_agent; probably-human units keep their group (owner, visitor). The validation set is every session that holds a mixed replay or a unit of agent_group, with all of its units; the rest is the dev set (S3.7). A mixed replay is an owner's session that agent units cover in part: at least the model's min_actions action segments, some inside the agent units and some outside (cake-ph-eval/mixed_eval.py).

untrusted._about: S9.2's training set gives each unit its truth and how strong it is (truth_strength). The site owner's presumed humans (owner true, truth_strength one of owner_strengths) are the group owner_presumed, weak answers: of the 11 owner units the user labelled on 2026-11-13, 9 were agents (research note 22), so they are reported on their own and left out of the human pools, the calibration and the threshold fits. The units the user labelled are the group user_labelled (people and agents).

layers._about: The table of what each part of Agent Cake finds alone and together (GOAL G7). halves: where evidence is read (env_rules.json legend). A configuration keeps the halves it lists: the page half is cake.js in the page (its environment signals, its User-Agent and the behaviour of its events), the collector half is the collect endpoint (the upload requests' headers, signatures and network), the server half is the site's server (the page request's headers, signature and Sec-Purpose).

reasons._about: Reason ids the tables count: the automated-browser sentence of D17 (A6) and the crawler-like weak signal (T22, A9).
